title: Make the changes, then walk once
statement: Make the changes and run the quicker checks before one full walk-through of a lesson, rather than walking, failing, patching and walking again.
example: The rule came after two cycles of walking, failing and patching were stopped.
detail: In a rebuild of a reading lesson, a "changes-first, then one walk" discipline started formally at tick 30, after two walk-fail-patch-walk cycles (journeys 32 and 33) were stopped: from then on a fan-out of the driver lens and the verifiers ran before the single walk (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0222-g3-l4-l1-parity-rebuild-2026-09-17-to-21.qmd`). The walks are runs of a Playwright-based walker (the same file).

evidence.quote: **"Changes-first, then one walk" discipline** (memory `changes-first-then-one-walk`) started formally at tick 30
two walk-fail-patch-walk cycles (journeys 32/33): a driver-lens + verifier fan-out runs BEFORE the single walk from tick 30 onward.
